surface_mechanism_description: The formation of the interfacial oxide layer in PEALD HfO2 films is attributed to the difference in the surface oxidation rate of the oxygen reactants used. During the initial stage of oxidation, layer-by-layer growth on the Si surface occurs. In the case of PEALD, the oxidation of the Si substrate by oxygen plasma retards relatively compared to ALD using water, resulting in the simultaneous deposition of HfO2 film and oxidation of the Si substrate, leading to the formation of Hf silicate and SiO2 in the interfacial layer. The existence of Hf silicate in the interfacial layer contributes to a higher dielectric constant than SiO2.
evidence: Though the mechanisms involved in the formation of silicate in PEALD are not well understood, it is postulated that the formation of Hf silicate in the interfacial layer of PEALD HfO2 films may be attributed to the difference in the surface oxidation rate of the oxygen reactants used. During the initial stage of oxidation, some reports presented the evidence for layer-by-layer growth on the Si surface. Three-dimentional island growth has also been claimed to occur under certain oxidation conditions. In the initial stage of ALD HfO2 films, the surface oxidation onto the Si substrate occurs very rapidly by water. Therefore, since the deposition of HfO2 films actually proceeds on the SiO2 layer, not on the Si substrate, the interfacial layer consists mainly of SiO2 in the ALD process using water. On the contrary, in case of PEALD HfO2 films, the oxidation of the Si substrate by oxygen plasma retards relatively compared to ALD using water. As a result, the deposition of the HfO2 film and the oxidation of the Si substrate occur onto the Si substrate at the same time in the early deposition stage. Thus, the interfacial layer of PEALD HfO2 films is made up of Hf silicate and SiO2. Another probable explanation for the difference in interface composition is that energetic species can promote the mixing of atoms near the surface by momentum transfer and by enhanced diffusion. The existence of Hf silicate in the interfacial layer would be helpful for obtaining a higher effective dielectric constant because the Hf silicate has a higher dielectric constant than SiO2.
